metadata.methods_description: Participants completed 120 trials per session in a 2 (social, non-social) x 3 (watch-neutral, watch-negative, reappraise-negative) design, rating arousal and valence for each image. tDCS was delivered with a Starstim 8 system (2 mA for 20 min active; ramp-up/down only for sham) to left or right dlPFC. EEG was recorded with a 32-channel montage on a 64-channel QuickCap and a Neuroscan SynampsRT amplifier at 1000 Hz. Preprocessing used EEGLAB and ERPLAB: 0.1-30 Hz filtering, downsampling to 250 Hz, mastoid re-referencing, ICA artifact removal, epoching and averaging.

citation_details.title: SPERA: Spherical Prior EEG Foundation Model with Geometry- and Frequency-Aware Latent Prediction
citation_details.author: Minsu Kim, Ye-Sung Kim, Hye-seon Jeon, Wooseok Hyung, Joshua Lee, Chang-Hwan Im
citation_details.abstract: Electroencephalography (EEG) provides a non-invasive measure of ongoing neural activity, but building general-purpose EEG models remains challenging due to the heterogeneity of subjects, devices, and electrode montages. Existing EEG foundation models predominantly rely on reconstruction-based objectives defined on the observed signal, which contains both neural and non-neural components. We introduce the Spherical Prior EEG Representation Architecture (SPERA), an EEG foundation model that adopts the joint-embedding predictive architecture (JEPA) to predict in latent space. SPERA introduces a Legendre-polynomial spatial prior, incorporated into attention to encode varying scalp electrode geometries. Two further components adapt the model to EEG: factorized temporal and spatial attention interleaved with periodic full-attention blocks, and a relational spectral regularizer aligning latent similarity structure with spectral views. Pretrained on approximately 80,000 hours of EEG from 29,04
